title: Competitive Field Probe: Regional Model Readiness & Evidence Backlog
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Objective: run a two-week, lightweight field probe that collects verifiable signals about competing model availability, latency variance, fallback readiness, and quantization compatibility across three target regions (NA, EU, APAC). The probe will produce an evidence backlog consumable by Sourcing, Runtime, and Sales to de-risk procurement and inform routing policies. Scope: create standardized request templates, synthetic workloads representing SMB and enterprise RAG traffic, a reproducible test harness, and a first tranche of region-specific findings (3–5 models per region). Deliverables: 1) evidence backlog (ranked signals), 2) reproducible probe harness in the signal-lab, 3) short recommendation memo for routing fallback rules and procurement gating, 4) ops playbook for surfacing availability regressions to SRE and Sales.
acceptance_criteria: Probe harness can run end-to-end in <2 hours for all three regions using existing credits
Collected signals include per-model latency, error rate, max-seq support, quantization availability, and documented failure modes
Evidence backlog contains at least 9 unique model-region entries (3 models x 3 regions) with timestamped runs
Recommendation memo includes clear thresholds for automatic fallback and procurement alerting
Hand-off session scheduled with SRE, Sourcing, and Sales and recording linked in ticket
tasks: Define workload templates (short-chat, long-context RAG query, embedding batch) and expected performance anchors
Instrument probe harness (signal-lab repo) to capture token-level latency and structured error codes
Select candidate models per region and document provenance, license, and quantization notes
Run baseline probes during off-peak and peak windows and collect percentile latency distributions
Curate evidence backlog entries, tag with confidence level, and prioritize top 6 signals for action
Draft recommendation memo and propose fallback thresholds for routing policy experiments
Schedule cross-functional review and capture feedback for iteration

notes: This ticket intentionally targets breadth (region x model) with a small, reproducible harness rather than a full benchmarking run. Goal is actionability: produce prioritized signals that map directly to routing/fallback rules or procurement triggers.
